s: Daniel and his friends are taken to Babylon and stay faithful to God's food laws.
Daniel interprets Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a great statue: God will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed.
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to worship the golden statue and are thrown into the furnace. They sing God's praise in the flames, and an angel saves them.
Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a great tree. He is humbled until he praises the God of heaven.
At Belshazzar's feast a hand writes on the wall. Daniel reads it, and that night the king is killed.
Daniel keeps praying to God despite the king's decree and is thrown into the lions' den, but God shuts the lions' mouths.
Daniel's vision of four beasts and one like a son of man coming with the clouds, given an everlasting kingdom.
The vision of the ram and the goat, explained by Gabriel.
Daniel confesses Israel's sins. Gabriel reveals the seventy weeks until an anointed one.
After fasting, Daniel sees a heavenly messenger.
The kings of the north and the south.
Michael will arise, and those who sleep in the dust will awake, some to everlasting life.
Daniel, a young man, saves the virtuous Susanna from false witnesses.
Daniel exposes the priests of Bel and kills the dragon, and is kept safe in the lions' den again.

3: Three young men refuse to worship an idol and are thrown into the furnace, but God keeps them safe. Their song of praise is still prayed by the Church.
6: Daniel keeps praying to God despite the king's law. God protects him from the lions.
7: Daniel sees one like a son of man receive an everlasting kingdom. Jesus often calls himself the Son of Man.
